questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: A laxative eases passage of ____ stool, while a purgative clears formed/preformed stool.
questions.exp: Laxative: formed stool; purgative: formed/preformed stool (Book p269)

questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: The use of a purgative is ____.
questions.exp: Purgative use: pre-op bowel cleaning (Book p269)

questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: At high doses, ____ behave similar to purgatives.
questions.exp: At high doses, laxatives behave similar to purgatives (Book p269)

questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: Match the term to its definition.
right: Dietary fibres that act as substrate for microorganisms
questions.exp: Probiotics = beneficial microorganisms; prebiotics = dietary fibres substrate; symbiotics = probiotics + prebiotics (Book p269)

questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: Which set lists probiotic examples?
questions.exp: Probiotic examples: bacillus clausii, lactobacillus, saccharomyces (Book p269)

questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: Prebiotic examples are psyllium husk, bran and ____.
questions.exp: Prebiotics: psyllium husk, bran, methylcellulose (Book p269)

questions.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
questions.q: Probiotics help constipation by ↑ stool formation → stretching & ____ of the large intestine.
questions.exp: ↑ stool formation → stretching & contraction of large intestine (Book p269)

questions.q: Bisacodyl, senna and cascara act by:
opts: Low-grade inflammation → nerve-ending irritation → ↑ intestinal contraction
Osmotic draw of water into the lumen → soft bulky stool
Surfactant action → ↓ stool surface tension → stool collapse
Direct (−) of intestinal Cl- channels → luminal water retention
questions.exp: Promotes low grade inflammation → irritation of nerve endings → ↑ contraction of intestine (Book p269)

questions.q: Stimulant laxatives take 6–8 hrs to act, hence they are taken at ____.
questions.exp: 6–8 hrs (hence taken at night) (Book p269)

questions.q: Atonic colon from continuous stretching is prevented by avoiding stimulant laxatives for more than ____ days.
questions.exp: Prevented by avoiding use for >10 days (Book p269)

questions.q: Hypokalemia as a stimulant-laxative side effect is tagged to ____.
questions.exp: Hypokalemia → bisacodyl (Book p269)

questions.q: Melanosis coli (black pigmentation of intestinal epithelium) is caused by senna and ____.
questions.exp: Melanosis coli → senna, cascara (Book p269)

questions.q: Stimulant laxatives are contraindicated in ____.
questions.exp: Contraindication: intestinal obstruction (Book p269)

questions.q: Castor oil is metabolized to ____ , the actual stimulant.
questions.exp: Castor oil → metabolized to ricinoleic acid → stimulant (Book p269)

questions.q: Match the osmotic laxative to its book fact.
right: Saline laxative C/I in renal failure
Non-digestible sugar used in hepatic encephalopathy
questions.exp: Mg salts C/I renal failure; Na salts C/I CHF; lactulose in hepatic encephalopathy; PEG DOC in IBS with constipation (Book p270)

questions.q: Non-digestible sugars are metabolized to ____ , which draw in water.
questions.exp: Metabolized to saturated fatty acids → draws in water (Book p270)

questions.q: The non-digestible sugars are ____ line for constipation because they are expensive.
questions.exp: 2nd line for constipation (expensive) (Book p270)

questions.q: In hepatic encephalopathy, lactulose makes intestinal pH acidic, converting NH3 to water-soluble ____ which is excreted.
questions.exp: NH3 → NH4+ (water soluble) → excreted (Book p270)

questions.q: The side effect of non-digestible sugars is ____.
questions.exp: Side effect: flatulence (Book p270)

questions.sec: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors
questions.q: Docusate sodium and docusate calcium are ____ that ↓ surface tension of stool so it collapses and passes easily.
questions.exp: Surfactants: ↓ surface tension of stool → stool collapses (Book p270)

questions.sec: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors
questions.q: Mineral oil is rarely used because of the risk of ____.
questions.exp: Risk of aspiration pneumonia → hence rarely used (Book p270)

questions.sec: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors
questions.q: Tenapanor blocks the ____ exchanger, increasing intestinal Na+ & H2O.
questions.exp: Blocks Na+/H+ exchanger → increases intestinal Na+ & H2O; use IBS with constipation (Book p270)

questions.sec: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors
questions.q: Lubiprostone stimulates type-2 ____ channels in intestinal epithelial cells → ↑ excretion of Cl- & H2O.
questions.exp: Stimulates type-2 Cl- channels → ↑ excretion of Cl- & H2O (Book p270)

questions.sec: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors
questions.q: Linaclotide and plecanatide increase Cl- & H2O secretion by:
questions.exp: Stimulate guanylate cyclase → ↑cGMP → stimulate CFTR → ↑ secretion of Cl- & H2O (Book p270)

questions.q: The opioid DOC for IBS with diarrhea (non-secretory) is ____.
questions.exp: Opioids: loperamide (DOC), diphenoxylate, difenoxin — IBS with diarrhea (non-secretory) (Book p271)

questions.q: Match the anti-diarrheal to its book fact.
right: μ & κ agonist + δ antagonist → IBS with diarrhea
IBS with diarrhea in females (S/E ischemic colitis)
questions.exp: Opioids → non-secretory IBS diarrhea; eluxadoline μ&κ agonist/δ antagonist; resins (cholestyramine, colesevelam, colestipol) → biliary diarrhea; alosetron → females, ischemic colitis (Book p271)

questions.q: Match the anti-diarrheal to its mechanism/use.
right: ↓ gastrin & VIP secretion → secretory diarrhea (HIV/DM/chemo), pancreatitis, dumping syndrome
Inhibits enkephalinase → ↑ enkephalin → diarrhoea in children
Inhibits CFTR → ↓ Cl- and water → HIV associated diarrhoea
questions.exp: Octreotide ↓gastrin & VIP, ↓GIT contraction/secretion; racecadotril ↑enkephalin; crofelemer inhibits CFTR (Book p271)

questions.q: The 5HT3 antagonist alosetron (IBS with diarrhea in females) has the side effect ____.
questions.exp: S/E: ischemic colitis (Book p271)

questions.q: Octreotide ↓ secretion of gastrin and ____ (vasointestinal peptide).
questions.exp: ↓ secretion of gastrin & vasointestinal peptide (VIP) (Book p271)

questions.q: Racecadotril inhibits enkephalinase, raising ____ (the endogenous opioid) — used for diarrhoea in children.
questions.exp: Inhibits enkephalinase → ↑ enkephalin (endogenous opioid) (Book p271)

questions.q: Crofelemer (HIV associated diarrhoea) inhibits ____ , decreasing Cl- and water.
questions.exp: Inhibits CFTR → ↓ Cl- and water (Book p271)

units.title: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics
units.sec: Laxatives vs Purgatives; Probiotics and Prebiotics · p269
units.guide: Laxative: formed stool, Rx constipation; purgative: formed/preformed, pre-op cleaning; high-dose laxatives ≈ purgatives. Probiotics = beneficial microbes (bacillus clausii, lactobacillus, saccharomyces); prebiotics = fibres (psyllium, bran, methylcellulose); symbiotics = both.

units.title: Stimulant Laxatives
units.guide: Bisacodyl/senna/cascara: low-grade inflammation → nerve irritation → ↑ contraction; 6–8 h → at night. S/E atonic colon (>10 days), hypokalemia (bisacodyl), melanosis coli (senna, cascara). C/I intestinal obstruction. Castor oil → ricinoleic acid.

units.title: Osmotic Laxatives
units.guide: Saline: Mg salts (C/I renal failure), Na salts (C/I CHF) — pre-op cleaning. Non-digestible sugars → saturated fatty acids draw water; 2nd line (expensive); lactulose in hepatic encephalopathy (NH3→NH4+); flatulence. PEG: DOC IBS with constipation.

units.title: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors
units.sec: Stool Softeners, Tenapanor and Chloride Secretors · p270
units.guide: Docusate Na/Ca: surfactants. Mineral oil: aspiration pneumonia risk. Tenapanor blocks Na+/H+. Lubiprostone: type-2 Cl- channels. Linaclotide/plecanatide: guanylate cyclase → cGMP → CFTR. All for IBS with constipation.

units.title: Anti-diarrheal Drugs
units.guide: Opioids (loperamide DOC) → non-secretory IBS diarrhea. Eluxadoline μ&κ agonist/δ antagonist. Resins → biliary diarrhea. Alosetron → females, ischemic colitis. Octreotide → secretory diarrhea (HIV/DM/chemo), pancreatitis, dumping. Racecadotril ↑enkephalin → children. Crofelemer inhibits CFTR → HIV diarrhea.
